_meta.purpose: Per-series baselines used by the Repair Diagnostician (Agent 10) to decide whether a finding is genuine drift or normal source behaviour. Mirrors data/playbook.md §2.2-2.3 in machine-readable form.
rules: Agents read this file. Agents do NOT modify it without human review.
When a finding contradicts a baseline here, raise an incident rather than silently disagreeing.
When this file and the LLM disagree, this file wins.

_staleness_measurement_warning: publish_lag_days below measures LAG FROM PERIOD-END (when does the source typically publish, relative to the period it describes) — it is NOT the same quantity as validation_report.json's staleness findings, which report `age_days` = days since the series' own reference DATE (FRED dates a monthly obs to the 1st of its reference month, a quarterly obs to the 1st of its reference quarter). Those two bases differ by up to a full period length. A GDP finding with age_days=147 is NOT '147 days late by this table's 60-day bea_quarterly ceiling' — quarter-start-dated series legitimately reach ~120-220 age_days across a healthy quarter. Use staleness_age_ceiling_days below (mirrors scripts/validator.py's EXPECTED_LAGS exactly, same units as age_days) when reasoning about a Staleness finding; use publish_lag_days only for the separate question of 'how many days after the period ended did the source actually publish.' Confusing the two produced real false-positive risk — see staleness_age_ceiling_days' own note.

bea_pce.note: PCE genuinely lags ~95 days at times; do NOT recommend action below 110 days

staleness_age_ceiling_days._note: Mirrors scripts/validator.py check_staleness()'s EXPECTED_LAGS dict exactly — same keys (raw_data.json series names), same units (age_days from the series' own reference date, not from period-end). Added 2026-08 after finding icsa/ccsa had ZERO staleness coverage (missing entry entirely) for a month-long live-site freeze, and that ~20 more series were silently unchecked due to a shape-handling bug in check_staleness() (fixed same pass — see CLAUDE.md). Live-verified against FRED directly (not just reasoned about) for the four highest-risk entries below before setting their ceilings; keep this list in sync if validator.py's dict changes, or an LLM reasoning from this file alone will reproduce the exact false-positive/false-negative mistakes already made and fixed once.
staleness_age_ceiling_days._tdsp_note: tdsp is a Federal Reserve Board series, NOT NY Fed like cc_delinq/mtg_delinq — live-verified 2026-08-26 that FRED itself shows 'Next Release Date: Not Available' for this series (genuinely irregular cadence, not comparable to the NY Fed HHDC series despite the shared 'household debt' category).

noise_floor_pp._units_note: Values are in the metric's natural units: pp for percentage-point series, points for sentiment indices, $/gal for gasoline.

shock_tracker_yoy_min_obs._note: YoY phases in update_shock_tracker need at least this many observations of the underlying series to compute pre/now without falling through to a hardcoded baseline. Mirrors CLAUDE.md Shock Tracker Data Contracts table.

benign_warnings._note: Warning patterns that are known-benign and should be downgraded to informational by the Diagnostician.
benign_warnings.patch_kpi_not_found_after_double_render: Renderer runs twice on the same HTML produce 'not found' warnings — labels already updated.
benign_warnings.umcsent_status_missing: umcsent entries without an explicit 'status' field are treated as 'final' for back-compat; not a bug.
benign_warnings.u_sector_mom_skip_low_obs: U_SECTOR_MOM rebuild SKIPPED when <10/13 sectors have ≥2 obs — chart shows stale data but renderer correctly refuses to compute spurious diffs.

model_routing._note: Which Claude model to use for which agent task. Read by _models.py / agents at startup. The Diagnostician uses Sonnet; Opus is reserved for higher-stakes reasoning (Stage 10b proposer, Stage 10c critique).
model_routing._critic_note: Two-LLM critique uses Opus for the second opinion — different family from the proposer reduces correlated reasoning errors.
